corrections.compiler_and_flags: GCC 14.2.1 20240910; build.sh configures CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release (CMake default -O3 -DNDEBUG) with -Wall -Wextra; BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON
corrections.claimed_speedup: Scenario 2 (iterations x repeats), 1 thread median 148 ns vs spdlog async 518 ns (3.5x) and spdlog sync 587 ns (4.0x) (derived from page data); 12 threads median 29.8 ns vs spdlog async 1802 ns and sync 1266 ns (google-benchmark Time averaged over threads)
corrections.caveats: Benchmark repo is by haclog's author (first-party run, but code and setup are public); haclog's 1-thread run has cv 49% (first two repeats 375 and 257 ns, mean 212 ns). The author's own analysis says haclog is fast only in the non-stress scenario 2: in scenario 1 (min-time, buffer full) it blocks and its efficiency drops significantly. Multi-thread Time is the benchmark's per-thread-averaged figure, not per-call latency. Same shootout ranks fmtlog, NanoLog and quill as fast or faster.

notes: Numbers match the report files exactly. Upgrade rests on build.sh Release build type standing in for explicit flags (lzbench precedent of public build files); downgrade to C if the orchestrator wants explicit -O flags printed.
